question.problem: If $\operatorname{ln}⁡x=9-5\operatorname{ln}⁡x$, then what is the value of  $x?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we simplify our equation by collecting the like logarithmic terms, and isolating the logarithm, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡x & =9-5\operatorname{ln}⁡x \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡x+5\operatorname{ln}⁡x & =9 \\ (1+5)\operatorname{ln}⁡x & =9 \\ 6\operatorname{ln}⁡x & =9 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡x & =\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

To remove the logarithm, we exponentiate both sides of the equation. The logarithm is a natural logarithm, which means its base is $e.$ So, we use a base of $e$ for the exponentiation as well:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡x & =\frac{3}{2} \\ {e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡x} & ={e}^{3/2}\end{aligned}
$$

Since exponentiation is the inverse function of the logarithm, we get ${e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}=x.$ 

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={e}^{3/2} \\ x & =\sqrt{{e}^{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$
